rows.answer:
The punishment for defamation is simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service, under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860) [1][8].

Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 replaces sections 499 [7], 500 [8], 501 and 502 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

rows.answer:
A person accused of a non-bailable offence may be released on bail by an officer in charge of a police station or by a Court other than the High Court or Court of Session, unless there appear reasonable grounds for believing that the person has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, or unless the person is a cognizable offender previously convicted of an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for seven years or more, or previously convicted on two or more occasions of a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment for three years or more but less than seven years under Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 437 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973) [1][2][7].
